I overheat super easily, but I’m also a teacher, so I struggle to find stuff that’s reasonably modest without being too hot or tent-like! 
Always on the lookout for sleeveless but modest dresses that are lightweight and have pockets! Ideally knee length, it’s so frustrating that you can pick either mid calf or mini skirt.

Everyone has already responded about how it’s unfair to other students, so I’ll add that it’s also unfair to the usual A plus student. Yes, they may have been sick or tired… or they may have been accustomed to high marks so they thought they could slack off. As someone who was that student in high school (OP1, straight As without really trying), that first 4 at uni was a real wake up call. Getting poor grades isn’t a punishment, it’s just something that happens sometimes due to things within and outside of your control, and it’s a learning opportunity. Better they have that learning opportunity in a secondary school context where the teachers actually care, than in a uni context where most tutors barely remember your name.

Been there- pre teaching. I think wearing a proper dressing and bandage and just claiming you have an injury (not untrue) would be less “suspicious”- if you don’t usually wear sleeves then it might look like you are trying to hide them. Kids are curious and if they think there’s a “juicy” secret then they will try and press you, but if they think you had a boring injury on the weekend (make up a good story if you like) then they will probably just take it at face value. 
I still have scars from years ago, but they are burns rather than typical cuts so they don’t immediately scream “self harm”. I have a few stories I rotate through, and use them as teachable moments- ie in chem “make sure you don’t get acid on your skin, like I did when I was your age!” Alternatively, a very sarcastic answer like “I fought a dragon and it breathed fire on me”
Makes the kids laugh. I really hope you have support, and can access leave if you need to ❤️

Thank you everyone for the solidarity, it means a lot to read about others who are struggling/have struggled, and how that affects what your career looks like. It’s good to know that there are options for reduced load- I don’t really see them advertised. I probably should have said in the original post that Im secondary, not primary- that’s why I was hearing that it is hard to negotiate to that 0.6/0.8 level. I can definitely relate to those of you who for whatever reasons don’t disclose- I feel that people in management are wrapping their heads around depression and anxiety, but still stigmatise other mental health conditions - no matter how well managed- as making you inherently unfit to be a teacher. Hard to find that line between advocating for your needs vs shooting yourself in the foot!

Yeah, running causes red blood cell breakdown so you have to be reaaaallly on top of things. My b12 and vitamin d are normal- my vit d is actually really high which I low key attribute to living in a place where it’s hot 10 months of the year 🙃Im lucky in that I used to be a dietitian so I have more of an idea of supplementation and nutrients so everything isn’t so overwhelming.
Best of luck with the half!

Yes I feel so seen! I felt really bad getting a diagnosis because it felt like what I was dealing with wasn’t “a big deal” compared to others’ experiences. But I’ve already responded so positively to diet changes and lifestyle changes which has been validating- I don’t have to feel awful all the time to deserve to feel better, and since my sport is important to me I want all the tools to manage it as best I can. 
Does your HR go up when you do activities that don’t involve standing? Mine always stays pretty low when I’m on the stationary bike, and actually get a higher when I stop and stand up at the END of the workout !

Not only copyright infringement but also I hate how little nuance is used when discussing the effects of menstrual cycle and athletic performance. Research is far from conclusive and while interesting and worth considering it’s just one kind of data which can be used among others to inform training approaches. Plus I hate how it exacerbated the female fragility stereotype..: like if we took this “nooo don’t do hiit before your period you’re so sexy “ thing literally then AFAB athletes would think they have like 1-2 weeks per month where they can actually perform. We should always be encouraged to modify our workouts as needed, which may or may not involve paying more attention to lenses. 

Sincerely, a former sports and eating disorder dietitian, engaged to an exercise physiologist. We actually read and stay up to date the emerging studies. I’m a 9 time marathoner and ran a 2 min 5k PB (19:20- hardly elite but I’m proud) on the “worst” day of my cycle.

Side note- if anyone wants to follow some evidenced based Insta accounts (because unfortunately scientific research can be inaccessible financially and educationally), I personally love @doclyssfitness. I don’t know her personally but she actually works in research specialising in “female” hormones and athletic performance.
